t8.text: States: loading, offline, empty, errors, toasts

g6.text:
State rules

Loading: skeleton in the real layout, never a spinner page. Cached data shows at once with its age; skeleton only on very first load.
Offline vs asleep: no internet = grey banner, commands disabled with reason. Car asleep = amber line, commands still allowed (they queue + wake).
Signed out elsewhere: Honda allows one phone. Explain, keep the car picture, one button to sign in again.
Package expired: read-only data stays, remote actions replaced by one renew link.
Toast = result of something you just did (3 s, top, swipe up). Banner = ongoing condition (stays until fixed). Errors on a form = inline under the field, not a toast.

g5.text:
Onboarding rationale

Goal: first launch to unlocking the car in under 60 s.
3 intro slides max, skippable. Then only what the API needs: region, phone + password, SMS code.
Step 4 is the honest part: Honda binds an account to one phone. Signing in here signs the official app out. Say it before the SMS, not after.
Step 6 is the reward: the car appears in its real color (from /car/image) with plate. Feels like a key handover.
Step 7 lets the user pick body shape (pre-selected from the API model), style (shaded / line / Honda photo) and paint. Skippable.
Step 8 groups Face ID, notifications and Siri on one screen, each skippable. No permission prompt without a reason line.
Progress bar: 4 segments for sign-in steps only. Intro slides use dots.

g4.text:
Account, multi-car, sharing

Sign in once; token in Keychain, Face ID to reopen. Password goes only to Honda.
Multi-car: name on Home is the switcher. Swipe the car image left/right to change car. Widgets and Siri take a car ("Lock the City"); default = last used.
Shared cars show who shared them and only the actions you were given. Hidden actions are not shown greyed out.
Sharing: per-person permissions (location / lock / unlock / engine) + expiry. Unlock and engine need Face ID on the guest's device.
Devices: every signed-in device is listed; sign out one or all.

Open question: if Honda's API has no guest users, sharing needs our own backend holding the owner's token. That is a security decision, not a UI one.

g1.text:
Gesture map

Tap = safe, reversible (Lock, open a screen).
Swipe / scrub to choose, never tap-tap: swipe the car to change car or body shape; slide a knob for AC level and style; scrub a finger along the paint rail. Value changes live under the finger, haptic tick per stop, knob springs to the nearest stop on release. Taps and VoiceOver adjust (swipe up/down) still work.
Hold ~0.6 s = physical / risky (Unlock, Start engine). The pill fills under the thumb; release early cancels. Haptic: light tick at start, firm tap when armed.
Pull down on Home = wake the car + refresh. Not a reload: it sends a wake, then reads live data.
Swipe left on a notification = delete. Edge-swipe = back.
All primary controls live in the bottom 40% of the screen.

g2.text:
Async command pattern

1 Fire: button turns into its own progress ring at once. Haptic tick. No modal, no blocking.
2 Accepted: one calm line says the car got it ("Accepted · waiting for car").
3 Confirm: poll until the car reports the new state, then a success haptic and the headline changes.
Slow / car asleep: amber "Connection unstable — retrying". Keep the last known state visible. Only after all retries: "Couldn't reach car" + Try again.
The UI is optimistic in motion, honest in words: the headline only changes when the car confirms.

g3.text:
Siri flows

Every intent answers in one spoken sentence + a compact snippet, no app launch.
Read intents (Is it locked? Where is it?) run at once.
Physical intents (Unlock, Start) ask "Unlock your HR-V?" — Siri confirmation is the voice version of long-press.
Lock needs no confirm.
Slow car: Siri says "Sent. I'll notify you when it's done." and a push confirms later.
